name_reason: Fully compliant: data_fd2_ prefix (game global), battle_ domain (battle core table), descriptor 'combat_hit_shake_x_offset_table' accurately reflects both purpose (per-subframe horizontal shake offsets for the combat-hit cinematic) and data type (_table). The '_x' axis tag is meaningful (companion '_y' table at 0x52577), not address residue. No Ghidra address residue in name.
purpose: Const int32[6] of per-subframe horizontal screen-shake pixel displacements applied to the defender sprite during the combat-hit FIGANI cinematic.
logic_summary: Sole consumer fd2_execute_combat_hit_cinematic (@0x2939D) copies all 6 dwords to a stack-local int[6] in one REP MOVSD (0x293C8-0x293D4: MOV ECX,6; MOV ESI,0x5255F; MOVSD.REP -> 4-byte stride, 6 elements). A shake counter held in ESI is latched to 5 on each landed hit (0x29784 MOV ESI,0x5) and decays toward 0 (0x29A25 DEC ESI, gated by TEST ESI,ESI / JZ). Each subframe the local copy is indexed by ESI as a full signed dword and applied to the defender framebuffer pointer: player-attacker branch ADD EAX,[ESP+ESI*4+0x8] (+x, 0x2980F); enemy-attacker branch SUB EAX,[ESP+ESI*4+0x8] (-x, 0x29AE3). Because the counter starts at 5 (last element) and decays, the offsets play back 14->18->14->9->4->0, a recoil that peaks then settles.
element_semantics: Each element is a signed horizontal pixel displacement (in screen pixels, applied directly to the linear framebuffer pointer with no row-stride scaling) for one shake step. Indexed by the decaying ESI shake counter (5..0). Values = {0, 4, 9, 14, 18, 14}.
notes: Source comment (btltab2.c lines 163-187) is already precise, ASCII, evidence-backed, with no flux/phase language; verified against disassembly of fd2_execute_combat_hit_cinematic (REP MOVSD x6, ESI counter latched to 5 and decaying, ADD player/+x at 0x2980F, SUB enemy/-x at 0x29AE3, signed dword index, read-only with only DATA load 0x293CF + READ 0x293D4 xrefs). Existing Ghidra PLATE_COMMENT is consistent with this conclusion (states same const int32[6], same ESI/ADD/SUB/REP MOVSD semantics, same read-only xrefs, same values, companion table @0x52577), so plate left untouched. No source edit needed; staged set is the shard file only.
